name: Heifetz / Mirage
full_name: 'Heifetz' remote digital-control endovascular robotic system with 'Mirage' steerable catheter (as tested at Huashan Hospital, Fudan University)
group: Shanghai Qingzhi Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (supplier named in the article); evaluated by Department of Vascular Surgery, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University (J. Y. Tan, B. Yu)
target_anatomy: aortic arch branches and cerebral arteries (angiography)
haptics_leader: remote control box with a touch tablet outside the room, wireless link (article text, read 2026-11-08); force feedback N.R.
imaging_compat: X-ray fluoroscopy (tan2016_vivo abstract); Philips Allura Xper FD20 (article text, read 2026-11-08)
validation_detail: vascular model + cerebral angiography in Bama mini-pigs; no significant difference vs conventional technique in success, time or dose (tan2016_vivo abstract). Numbers from the article text: 5 mini-pigs of 28-40 kg; in the model 5 cannulations per target by 3 doctors (article text, read 2026-11-08)
key_numbers: model cannulation 17.7-31.5 s and 7.4-14.2 mGy per target; pig cannulation 29.1-60.3 s and 36.0-51.0 mGy per target; all targets cannulated (tan2016_vivo abstract)

sources.title: In vivo and in vitro experimental studies of remote digital control endovascular robotic system in interventional angiography

read_level_detail: abstract (tan2016_vivo, PMID 27866536); the article page was opened once on 2026-11-08 during the picture search
notes: Trademarked names (Heifetz, Mirage). Steerable-catheter design resembles Magellan-type systems (inference). D2 2026-11-19: catalogued without a picture (author's rule of 2026-11-19: a missing picture does not decide inclusion). The supplier, the animal count, the control interface and the X-ray system come from the article text as logged by the picture search of 2026-11-08 (P9_two_robots.md Sec. 2); that log also says the servo robot bends each joint of the catheter tip and advances and retracts catheter and guidewire (V-18 Control Wire). devices_driven, the mechanism cells and the devices-at-once code (1) still follow the abstract.
